sections.text:
1 Pisces enim deae Syriae sacri erant, quae a mythographis Veneri aequatur
(Eratosth., Catast., 38, etc.). Quod Theophilus discere potuit Edessae in sua patria
cuius incolae pisces Atargatidis praecipue venerabantur (Duval, Histoire d'Edesse,
p. 78. Cf. Pauly-Wissowa s. v., Dea Syria, c. 2242).
sections.en:
1 For fishes were sacred to the Syrian goddess, who is equated with Venus by mythographers
(Eratosthenes, Catasterismi, 38, etc.). This Theophilus could have learned at Edessa in his homeland,
whose inhabitants especially venerated the fishes of Atargatis (Duval, Histoire d'Edesse,
p. 78. Cf. Pauly-Wissowa s. v., Dea Syria, c. 2242).

summary.headline: Planetary Rulerships of Animals and Plants
summary.text: Astrological attributions of the Sun, Aphrodite, Mercury, and Moon to animals, birds, fishes, reptiles, domestic creatures, plants, fruits, spices, unguents, fibers, and alcoholic drinks. A footnote relates fishes to the Syrian goddess Atargatis, identified with Venus, citing Eratosthenes, Theophilus’s Edessan background, Duval, and Pauly-Wissowa.
